correctness.rationale: Over odd fields, the source splitting classification applies to the 3D nondegenerate bilinear-form Jordan algebra: every nontrivial nonzero-weight R has R^2=-Delta R, and up to phi=-R-Delta I, rank1 image line and rank2 unital kernel. Nontrivial image 1D subalgebra lines are exactly alpha^2=f(v,v), a nonsingular projective conic with q+1 F_q points independent of binary Witt type. Each such line excludes exactly its underlying v-direction among q+1 unital planes, leaving q complements. Thus rank1 count q(q+1), rank2 same under phi, and ranks0/3 only 0/-Delta I. For every finite extension replace q with q^m; summing log zeta yields (1-T)^-2(1-qT)^-2(1-q^2T)^-2. Independent exhaustive 3^9 coefficient-matrix checks for both discriminant classes over F3 found rank counts [1,12,12,1], and the source verifier was inspected separately; no extrapolation from finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Direct prior mathematical implication. The full 2018 Benito–Gubarev–Pozhidaev Example 13 is already a COMPLETE classification of every nonzero-weight RB operator on J_3(f) over characteristic !=2: up to phi, the one-dimensional image is a point on the explicit nonsingular projective conic and the kernel is a complementary unital plane. Over F_q every nonsingular projective conic has q+1 points, and for each image direction exactly one of the q+1 unital planes is noncomplementary. The q(q+1) rank-one count, its phi image, discriminant independence, extension counts and zeta are therefore immediate elementary finite-field corollaries of the stronger published theorem, even without matching displayed numerals. No independent new operator classification survives.

value.rationale: The finite-field rank distribution is a natural invariant, but here it is a short textbook enumeration of an already completely classified operator locus: smooth projective conic has q+1 rational points, one of the q+1 unital planes is excluded for each, and the involution doubles the count. No structurally new lemma, new parameter boundary, challenging exact classification, or independently motivated use of the precise census is established. The extension zeta is a formal exponentiation of the same elementary polynomial count. Correctness, easy reproducibility and absent exact numerals in the old paper cannot themselves confer mathematical value.
